classification: Source-backed conditional 100-percent wheel cutoff breach introduced by independent per-arc quantization; gameplay reachability and rendering impact have not been established.
trace: The source constructs actual impairment and projected increases separately, scales forecast to the available share, clips visible unrounded amounts using remaining, and subtracts those unrounded amounts. Each resulting amount is then independently rounded to the nearest thousandth for the serialized WheelArc.share. The browser adds each received share to the preceding SVG angle with no aggregate clamp.

For the representable nonnegative source values pain=0.3336, blood_loss=0.3336 and fear=0.3328, zero projected increase, and a displayed wheel, the mathematical 32-bit-float calculation gives rounded shares near 0.334, 0.334 and 0.333, whose sum exceeds one by approximately 0.001. All three are larger than the minimum visibility threshold. This is an evidence calculation, not an invocation of wheel_arcs, a product test, a JSON/DOM runtime observation, or proof that these precise values occur during play.

The selected historical renderer clips and directly advances its angular cursor using each unrounded amount. The current renderer instead crosses the JSON/DOM boundary after quantization. Historical source remains at its own selected revision; this comparison does not establish an unexecuted visual result.

Current color mapping uses a black fatigue segment, translucent grey encumbrance and yellow projected segments. Pinned bevy_color source shows to_hex includes an alpha byte when it is not 255; actual compiled feature selection and browser rendering remain unverified. Current source tests are preserved and were read only.
